mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which should boost consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4% but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month suggests increased economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows by more than 2% but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates inflationary pressures, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both HOUST and RSAFS are rising but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) suggests a strong labor market, which should boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE is falling and PAYEMS is rising but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% indicates a tightening monetary policy, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 2% but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month suggests reduced economic activity, which should negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by more than 1% but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.
